title: Review of c23's CIPS inhibitor finding on fresh seeds 4-5: no division replicates (0 persistent splits in 6 runs) and coarsening is slowed (40 -> 37 vs 56 -> 47 bodies over t=1500-3000), but it is not arrested: by t=6000 the inhibitor arm falls to 32 and the twin to 34
summary: Re-ran the finding's world.py at 128^2 with the inhibitor setting (DI 0.1, dI 0.01, kI 0.2, KI 0.5) and the matched kI=0 twin on seeds 4 and 5 (t=3000), and both arms on seed 4 to t=6000. Inhibitor: peak 43 bodies, 40 at t=1500 and 37 at t=3000 on both seeds, 6-7 merges. Twin: peak 73-80, 55-56 -> 46-47, 28-29 merges. Persistent splits 0 in all runs; the enzyme has no rim layer (rim/core 0.92). Continued to t=6000 (seed 4), the inhibitor arm keeps coarsening, 37 -> 33 -> 32 at t=3000/4500/6000 (11 merges in all), while the twin goes 46 -> 40 -> 34 (39 merges). So the inhibitor slows coarsening about 2-3x over t=1500-6000 rather than fixing a body size, and the two arms nearly converge by t=6000. The negative result about division stands.

observations.F: counts.txt: persistent splits 0 in 6/6 runs; inhibitor 40 -> 37 (seeds 4, 5) vs twin 56 -> 46 and 55 -> 47 over t=1500-3000; t=6000: inhibitor 32, twin 34

seeds_run.result: replicates to t=3000 (40 -> 37 vs 56 -> 46, 0 splits); at t=6000 not arrested (32 vs twin 34)

controls_run.F: noI/ and noI_T6000/ (matched kI=0 twins, same seeds, grid and duration)

verdicts.limitation: Weak only because the stated arrest at a fixed size does not hold past t=3000: counts keep falling slowly and the no-inhibitor twin nearly catches up by t=6000 (one seed for the long runs). The no-division part, the finding's main point, replicates on both seeds.
